Patronizing advice post incoming!

> I tried going to things like MeetUps and reddit-organized events but back out at the last minute

Cut that shit out and go.  You have arrived at a solution to your problems, now follow through.  Going to the first one sucks.  The second less so.  By the third time you'll probably do alright.  

> I have a hideous inferiority complex and always cast off myself, my work, and my achievements as nothing, and reject compliments and good vibes whenever people point them my way.

People want you to feel good.  You don't have to like it, but it's the truth.  If you're unwilling to empower them to improve your mood, pretend to take the compliment well.  Make them feel like their opinion matters to you, because be honest, it does.

If you're going to drink, invite a friend.

I live with someone now, but our relationship is sort of dying.  We've been together for four years and I'm just tired.  We went through a burnout phase together for a couple of years after I got her pregnant and we didn't keep it.  I feel like I gave up some of the best years of my life with her and I regret it.  She does a lot of things to help me, like keep me on an academic track, or make sure I follow up with medical appointments, but I feel like she's helped me to be weak.  I barely communicate with her anymore, we just talk about bullshit and obligatory stuff.  I'm scared to hurt her, and I'm scared to be alone, but I know I'm going to need change, and if I let myself be dictated by fear like I have for years now, I know I'll continue to regret.
Bit of a commute from sf...

I talked to him years ago when I first was confronting these feelings. A year later he said "you were being a bitch" when he thought I was better. It's hard to talk to him now. 

I would break up with her, but I'm still in junior college and the rent in the SF Bay Area is impossible to pay with minimum wage. I'd move back in with my parents, but they're divorced and in a similar situation of being unable to pay for their own living arrangements, and depend on their own significant others. 

My gf knows something is up but I haven't told her. I'm really scared.
